reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that draft picks are not static assets but conditional financial instruments akin to options. Each protection introduces a boundary condition on the underlying asset’s value, creating a payoff structure that mirrors option theory. The valuation problem becomes one of estimating the expected value of this conditional asset under uncertainty. The protection scheme space grows exponentially with the number of protected positions, implying combinatorial complexity in assessing trade value. A Bayesian approach allows updating beliefs about pick value based on observed trades, while a state-transition framework models how protection rules evolve over time. The failure mode arises when new protection types emerge beyond historical precedent, rendering models inapplicable.
